title: `round` rounds half up on the double's shortest decimal; `bround` half even
verdict: `round(x)`: `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO`; `round(x, d)` on the decimal text: `round(2.675, 2)` is 2.68
description: `round(x, d)` on a double turns it into a `BigDecimal` from its shortest decimal text (Scala's `BigDecimal(d)`, `Double.toString`) and rounds that `HALF_UP`, then converts back. So `round(x)` is half away from zero (`round(2.5)` 3, `round(-2.5)` -3, `round(0.5)` 1), and `round(x, d)` rounds the decimal the double prints as, not its binary value: `round(2.675, 2)` is 2.68, `round(0.285, 2)` 0.29, `round(1.005, 2)` 1.01, where the binary values lie below the halves. Negative digits work (`round(1250, -2)` 1300). Integer `round` and `bround` keep the type, so negative digits can overflow it: `round(127y, -1)` (a `TINYINT`) raises `ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` under ANSI and wraps to -126 without it. NaN and ±inf come back unchanged; a rounded negative value that reaches zero is 0.0 (`round(-0.4)`). `d` must be a constant.
`bround` is the same with `HALF_EVEN` (`bround(2.5)` 2, `bround(0.285, 2)` 0.28). `round` of a `FLOAT` stays `FLOAT`.

`floor` and `ceil` of a double return `BIGINT`, not a double: they saturate without ANSI (`floor(1e20)` is 2⁶³ - 1), raise `ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` for ±inf and values past 64 bits under ANSI, and give 0 for NaN in both modes (SP-5). `floor(x, d)` returns a decimal.
reference: `round` with `rounding: TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` (#335), the only value the model accepts, to `d` digits with DuckDB's formula on the binary value (`x · 10ᵈ` rounded, then divided), so `round(2.675, 2)` is 2.67. `floor` and `ceil` return the double. Spark's `round(x)` is native; to `d` digits it differs where the decimal text sits on a half the binary value misses, and `floor`, `ceil` need a cast and guards.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
